summary: Continue the existing SupportIQ customer, IT-agent, and administrator portals and API, with local development and testing using the installed XAMPP MariaDB (MySQL-compatible) server as the first milestone. Keep Azure deployment as a later optional phase, using Azure services only when that phase is approved.

workspaceSignals.decisionReason: The workspace already contains a React/Vite frontend, an Express API, local development scripts, and persistent SQLite data; extend the app for the installed XAMPP MariaDB server rather than recreating it.

questions.question: Which programming language for SupportIQ Web Portal?
questions.rationale: The frontend uses TypeScript TSX files and a TypeScript configuration.

questions.question: Which frontend framework for SupportIQ Web Portal?
questions.rationale: The workspace includes React, React Router, Vite, and the Vite React plugin.

questions.question: Describe the features or API routes for SupportIQ Web Portal.
questions.answer: Preserve the three role-based portals: customers can use a support-only assistant, contact IT, create requests with attachments, track progress, and rate support; agents can triage and reply to tickets; administrators can review tickets and conversations, monitor service metrics, reassign or join conversations, and manage approved automated replies. Keep local development/testing first and Azure deployment optional and later.
questions.rationale: These capabilities are reflected in the existing portals and the previously recorded project requirements; the requested milestone order is local first, Azure later.
questions.recommendedChoice: Preserve the three role-based portals: customers can use a support-only assistant, contact IT, create requests with attachments, track progress, and rate support; agents can triage and reply to tickets; administrators can review tickets and conversations, monitor service metrics, reassign or join conversations, and manage approved automated replies. Keep local development/testing first and Azure deployment optional and later.

questions.question: Which programming language for SupportIQ API?
questions.rationale: The existing API is Node.js with Express, implemented in JavaScript. Confirm whether to target TypeScript or choose another supported backend language before proceeding.

questions.question: Which framework for SupportIQ API?
questions.rationale: The existing API entry point imports Express and mounts the current authentication, ticket, bot, admin, and upload routes.

options.label: Node.js with Express
options.description: Keep the existing Express API and route structure

questions.question: Describe the features or API routes for SupportIQ API.
questions.answer: Preserve role-based customer, IT-agent, and administrator access; private ticket and conversation APIs; replies and status/assignee changes; ratings and service metrics; support-only assistant responses and escalation; admin-managed knowledge and canned replies; secure attachments; and persistent activity history. Use the installed XAMPP MariaDB (MySQL-compatible) server and local file storage for the local-first milestone; consider PostgreSQL and Blob Storage only in a separately approved Azure phase.
questions.rationale: The existing API and previous requirements describe these capabilities; XAMPP MariaDB and local attachment storage are available for the local-first milestone.
questions.recommendedChoice: Preserve role-based customer, IT-agent, and administrator access; private ticket and conversation APIs; replies and status/assignee changes; ratings and service metrics; support-only assistant responses and escalation; admin-managed knowledge and canned replies; secure attachments; and persistent activity history. Use the installed XAMPP MariaDB (MySQL-compatible) server and local file storage for the local-first milestone; consider PostgreSQL and Blob Storage only in a separately approved Azure phase.

questions.question: Which data stores does your app need?
questions.rationale: Use the installed XAMPP MariaDB server and local files for the local-first phase. PostgreSQL and Blob Storage are proposed only for a later Azure phase; Blob Storage is needed for ticket attachments.

options.label: No datastore required
options.description: The app does not persist data or use storage, queues, or caches
